Workday (`wor`) + organisational (`ga`) workflows layered on top of [`rimir/cascade-palette`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-cascade-palette) and [`rimir/kind`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-kind). Demonstrates two integration patterns: (1) cp's sticky-context mechanism — pin people during a meeting, then watch context-aware views narrow to topics / tasks / notes involving the pinned set; and (2) conversation-centric verbs over a kind data model — take a call (creates a running conversation and drills into it), then surface and create the work items / topics in the context of its participants.

The plugin is intentionally small. It demonstrates the integration pattern; bring your own data model (kind, orga-data-model, hand-rolled tags) and adapt the filters via the three shipped config tiddlers to match your fields.

## Key features

- **`Take call from this person`** action — Space on a person row fires the verb: **creates a running `conversation`** (a `rimir/kind` instance) parented to the person, with that person as participant, `planned-at: now` and a `Conversation at <date time>` caption, then **drills into the new conversation** — its action menu on top, and popping out reveals the person's *Referenced by…* conversation list, then wherever you came from. Palette stays open (`ca-after-fire: keep`). Uses cp's `drill-sequence` message + kind's reverse-nav + create procedures. Surfaces on rows with `kind.type: person` AND on any tiddler tagged `Person`.
- **`In context of participants…`** action — on a `conversation` row, drills into the open work items and topics referencing the conversation's participants (teams expanded to member persons). Projects / tasks / todos clustered by role — *Waiting for*, *Assignee*, *Stakeholder* — and stakeholder *Topics* in their own cluster, each sorted soonest-actionable first (done / archived excluded). The same drill carries **New Project / Task / Todo / Topic…** rows: type a caption and ↵ to create one parented to the conversation, with the participants as stakeholders — it reappears in its cluster on the spot.
- **`Start meeting`** leader — bound to `m`. Clears the sticky context and opens the *Pick attendees* view.
- **`Pick attendees`** view — checkbox-style multiselect. Each row carries ☑/☐ mirroring whether that person is currently in sticky context. Enter toggles in/out. Pinned rows float to the top. Esc closes the picker; the populated context survives.
- **`Topics for context`** view — worked example of a context-aware view. Narrows to topics whose `stakeholders` field contains at least one pinned tiddler. Declares `ca-view-context-aware: yes` so the view pill paints an indigo badge when context is non-empty. Override `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-stakeholder-field` to match your data model.

## Prerequisites

- TiddlyWiki ≥ 5.4.0
- [`rimir/cascade-palette`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-cascade-palette) ≥ 0.0.124 — provides sticky-context + the view machinery as before (0.0.96–0.0.98), plus the `rimir-cascade-palette-drill-sequence` message (0.0.124) that `Take call` uses to create-then-land-in-context. Without 0.0.124 the `Take call` landing falls back to a no-op (the conversation is still created).
- [`rimir/kind`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-kind) ≥ 0.1.70 — **required** for `Take call` and `In context of participants…` (they create / list `kind` instances and reuse kind's reverse-nav + create procedures). A `conversation` type plus `project` / `task` / `todo` / `topic` / `person` / `team` types with the expected fields (`participants`, `parent`, `stakeholder`, `assignee`, `waiting-for`, `status`) must exist in your wiki. The `Pick attendees` / `Topics for context` flows still work tag-based without kind.

## Quick start

1. Install `rimir/cascade-palette` 0.0.124+, `rimir/kind` 0.1.70+ and this plugin. Restart.
2. Open the palette (Ctrl-Space). The Context pill strip is empty.
3. On any person row, Space → *Take call from this person*. A running `conversation` is created parented to the person, and the palette drills into it: you land on the conversation's action menu. From there, drill *In context of participants…* to see (or inline-create) the work items / topics involving the participants. Press **Esc** to pop back to the person's conversation list, then to where you came from.
5. For a multi-person meeting, type `m` (leader) → *Pick attendees* view opens. Enter on each attendee toggles in/out of context; view stays open; ☑/☐ updates live; pinned rows float to the top. **Esc** returns to the view you were in when you pressed `m` (the picked attendees stay in sticky context).
6. Shift-`C` clears the sticky context.

## Configuration

Three shadow config tiddlers let you adapt to your data model without forking:

- `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-stakeholder-field` — default `stakeholders`. The field *Topics for context* reads to find pinned people. If your topics use `stakeholder` (singular), `assignee`, `owner`, etc., change it here.
- `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-roots-filter` — default `[all[tiddlers]has[stakeholders]]`. Base "topics" candidates. If you have a typed model, scope to it: e.g. `[all[tiddlers]field:kind.type[topic]]`.
- `$:/config/rimir/worga/attendees-roots-filter` — default unions kind-typed and tag-typed persons, both with `!is[system]` so kind's self-describing type-definition tiddlers stay out of the picker.

## Adding your own context-aware view

```
title: $:/your/views/whatever
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view
ca-view-name: My narrowed view
ca-view-context-aware: yes
ca-view-roots: [all[tiddlers]has[<your-field>]] :filter[<currentTiddler>get[<your-field>]enlist-input[] :intersection[enlist<sticky-context-list>]]
```

The badge appears when sticky context is non-empty AND `ca-view-context-aware: yes`. The narrowing happens in the filter — there's no engine-level auto-narrow.

## Adding your own toggle-multiselect

For a checkbox-style multiselect view (the pattern *Pick attendees* uses):

```
title: $:/your/views/multiselect
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view
ca-view-name: Pick X
ca-view-roots: [all[tiddlers]field:kind.type[YOUR-TYPE]!is[system]]
ca-view-sort: custom
ca-view-sort-key: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[0]else[1]addsuffix<currentTiddler>]
ca-view-row-icon: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[☑]else[☐]]
ca-view-after-fire: stay
ca-view-row-actions: <$action-sendmessage $message={{{ [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[rimir-cascade-palette-unpin-context]else[rimir-cascade-palette-pin-context]] }}} title=<<currentTiddler>>/>
```

Two patterns coordinate: the row-icon + sort-key give visual state; the inline-filter `$message` toggles per row. Enter on any row pins or unpins; the palette stays open between toggles thanks to `ca-view-after-fire: stay`.

|!Version |!Date |!Changes |
|0.0.10 |2026-06-09 |''Conversation-centric verbs over a kind data model'' (`actions/take-call.tid` rewrite + new `actions/conversation-context.tid` + `macros.tid`). Needs `rimir/kind` ≥0.1.70 and `rimir/cascade-palette` ≥0.0.124. ''(1) "Take call from this person" reworked.'' Was: clear context → pin → jump to //Topics for context//. Now: ''creates a running `conversation`'' kind instance (parent + participant = the person, `planned-at: now`, dated `Conversation at …` caption via `kind.apply-defaults-to` + `kind.finalize-create`), then fires the new `rimir-cascade-palette-drill-sequence` message to ''drill into it'' — the conversation's action menu lands on top, with the person's //Referenced by…// conversation list (via `worga.call-conversations`, reusing kind's reverse-nav) as the pop-target. Still a `leaf` with `ca-after-fire: keep`. ''(2) New "In context of participants…" action'' on `conversation` rows: a drill over the open work items + topics referencing the conversation's participants (teams expanded to member persons via `members`). `worga.context-items` emits role-clustered rows — //Waiting for// / //Assignee// / //Stakeholder// for project/task/todo, plus stakeholder //Topics// — each date-sorted soonest-first, done/archived (or `completed-date`-bearing) excluded; reuses kind's `referencing-instances` / `resolve-ref` / `instance-row-json`, no reverse-ref logic duplicated. ''(3) Inline create'' in that same drill: four bind-less `ca-kind:text` rows (//New Project / Task / Todo / Topic…//) whose `ca-on-commit` calls `worga.create-in-context` with `<<picked>>` (typed caption) + `<<parent-picked>>` (the conversation) — sets parent = conversation, stakeholders = participants, caption = typed, applies defaults, derives the title from the kind's title-formula; the drill recomputes so the new item appears in its cluster. ''Touches:'' `actions/take-call.tid`, `actions/conversation-context.tid` (new), `macros.tid`, `readme.tid`, `README.md`, `doc/overview.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow / Macro tiddlers + a new action tiddler — restart required. |
|0.0.9 |2026-06-08 |''Pick attendees: sort unpinned rows alphanumerically by displayed caption (macros.tid + views/pick-attendees.tid).'' 0.0.5's `ca-view-sort-key` appended `<currentTiddler>` — the row ''title'' — so within the pinned / unpinned tiers rows sorted by title while the list ''displays'' captions (caption-then-title lens), making the order look random. New `worga.attendee-sort-key` function (in `macros.tid`) keys each row as `<tier> <caption>`: tier `0` for pinned (in `sticky-context-list`) / `1` otherwise, then the row's `caption` (falling back to title), so pinned still float to the top and everything else sorts alphanumerically by what's shown. `pick-attendees.tid` now sets `ca-view-sort-key: [function[worga.attendee-sort-key],<currentTiddler>]`. ''Touches:'' `macros.tid`, `views/pick-attendees.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow tiddlers only — restart required. |
|0.0.8 |2026-05-31 |''Docs only — calls out the view-history back-stack landing in cascade-palette 0.0.98 (readme.tid + README.md).'' Pre-0.0.98, after pressing `m` (Start meeting) or firing "Take call from <person>", Esc out of the resulting workflow view (Pick attendees / Topics for context) would close the palette and lose the side-quest context. cp 0.0.98 adds a per-session in-memory view-history stack; action/leader-initiated `set-view` jumps push a back-frame; bare Esc at root depth pops it before falling through to close. Only the view-jump unwinds — pinned attendees and the cleared/non-cleared sticky context from the same action chain stay (the call or meeting is still happening; the user just changed their mind about looking at this view). Worga's Quick start, dependency table, and shipped views section now document this — `m` is the canonical entry point for "Pick attendees with Esc-out" and `Take call` is the canonical entry point for "Topics for context with Esc-out". No tiddler-level changes; minimum cp dependency bumped to 0.0.98 in readme (the back-stack only fires when cp itself was updated). ''Touches:'' `readme.tid`, `README.md`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. No JS, no shadow tiddler changes; restart only needed to pick up the bumped readme. |
|0.0.7 |2026-05-31 |''Pick attendees toggle action rewritten as a single $action-sendmessage with inline-filter `$message` (views/pick-attendees.tid).'' 0.0.5/0.0.6 used two mutually-exclusive `<$list>` widgets to dispatch pin vs unpin. The list-iteration approach didn't fire reliably from `ca-view-row-actions` (Enter on a row didn't toggle even after the cp 0.0.96 ca-view-after-fire fix). Switched to a single `<$action-sendmessage $message={{{ [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[rimir-cascade-palette-unpin-context]else[rimir-cascade-palette-pin-context]] }}} title=<<currentTiddler>>/>` — one widget, one filter evaluated at fire time picking the right message name. Same `title` parameter works for both messages so the disambiguation is purely in `$message`. Pattern matches the simple `<$action-navigate $to=<<currentTiddler>>/>` shape that cp's built-in tree views (by-namespace, by-parent, by-date) use for `ca-view-row-actions` — single action widget, no nested conditional flow. ''Touches:'' `views/pick-attendees.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow tiddler only — restart required. |
|0.0.6 |2026-05-31 |''Exclude system tiddlers from `attendees-roots-filter` (config/attendees-roots-filter.tid).'' 0.0.5's fix changed the broken `get[kind.type]match[person]` chain to `field:kind.type[person]`, but the new filter also matches the kind plugin's TYPE DEFINITION tiddler at `$:/config/rimir/kind/types/person`: kind self-describes — its type tiddlers carry the very `kind.type` value they define. So the filter returned BOTH the type def AND every actual person instance, surfacing "person" alongside "Liliya Miertzschke" in the picker. Added `!is[system]` to both filter clauses: `[all[tiddlers]field:kind.type[person]!is[system]] [all[tiddlers]tag[Person]!is[system]]`. Type defs live under `$:/config/...` (system), real person instances don't, so the predicate cleanly separates them. ''Touches:'' `config/attendees-roots-filter.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow tiddler only — restart required. Companion to cascade-palette 0.0.96 which finally makes `ca-view-after-fire: stay` (the view-level keep-open this view was relying on) work. Without 0.0.96 the toggle on Enter fires but the palette closes anyway. |
|0.0.5 |2026-05-31 |''Pick attendees becomes a real multiselect — checkbox row icons, pinned-first sort, Enter toggles in or out.'' Three changes, one bug fix. ''(1) Fixed broken roots filter (config/attendees-roots-filter.tid).'' Was `[all[tiddlers]has[kind.type]get[kind.type]match[person]] [all[tiddlers]tag[Person]]` — the first clause's `get[kind.type]` REPLACES titles with the field value "person", so the filter returned the literal string `"person"` as a row instead of actual person tiddlers. Fixed with `field:kind.type[person]` which keeps titles intact AND filters by value: `[all[tiddlers]field:kind.type[person]] [all[tiddlers]tag[Person]]`. Same broken pattern was in worga's `take-call.tid` `ca-applies` filter but THAT one is fine because ca-applies just checks "non-empty result = applies" — the result content doesn't matter there. ''(2) Pin-state row icon (views/pick-attendees.tid `ca-view-row-icon`).'' `[enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[☑]else[☐]]` — pinned rows show ☑, unpinned show ☐. The `then`/`else` filter operators are TW's "replace input if non-empty / replace input if empty" pair — chains directly off `match<currentTiddler>` returning [currentTiddler] when in the list, [] when not. ''(3) Pinned-first sort (`ca-view-sort: custom` + `ca-view-sort-key`).'' Sort key per row: `[enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[0]else[1]addsuffix<currentTiddler>]` → produces "0<title>" for pinned, "1<title>" for unpinned. localeCompare puts "0" before "1", so pinned float to the top; alphabetic order is the natural tiebreaker within each group. ''(4) Enter toggles instead of pin-only (`ca-view-row-actions`).'' Two mutually-exclusive `<$list>` blocks, each iterates exactly once or not at all: list 1 with filter `[<currentTiddler>] -[enlist<sticky-context-list>]` fires `pin-context` only when current row is NOT pinned; list 2 with filter `[enlist<sticky-context-list>] +[match<currentTiddler>]` fires `unpin-context` only when current row IS pinned. Single line per field per TW's `.tid` parser. The cp engine evaluates `ca-view-row-actions` as a filter first and falls back to the raw string when filter eval produces nothing — the `<$list>` wikitext goes through the fallback path and is dispatched as an action chain at fire time. ''Touches:'' `config/attendees-roots-filter.tid`, `views/pick-attendees.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow tiddlers only — restart required for the shadow updates to land. |
|0.0.4 |2026-05-31 |''`take-call` now also jumps to the "Topics for context" view after pinning (actions/take-call.tid).'' Symmetric with `start-meeting` (which jumps to "Pick attendees") — the action becomes a single-keystroke "I'm in a call with this person, show me the topics" macro instead of just pinning and leaving the user to switch views manually. Action chain is now three messages: `clear-context` → `pin-context` → `set-view: $:/plugins/rimir/worga/views/topics-for-context`. Hint updated. ''Touches:'' `actions/take-call.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow tiddler changed — restart required. |
|0.0.3 |2026-05-31 |''`take-call` keeps the palette open after firing (actions/take-call.tid).'' Added `ca-after-fire: keep` to mirror the same change on cp-core's `sticky-context-pin` / `-unpin` shadows (cascade-palette 0.0.95). Single-keystroke entry into a call now leaves the palette focused on the action menu so the user can follow up immediately (switch to "Topics for context", take notes, pin another attendee, etc.) without re-opening cp. ''Touches:'' `actions/take-call.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. Shadow tiddler changed — restart required. |
|0.0.2 |2026-05-30 |''Bug fixes: single-line `ca-actions` field values + correct `:intersection` per-topic predicate.'' Two corrections to 0.0.1. ''(1) Multi-line `ca-actions` / `ca-leader-actions` (take-call.tid + start-meeting.tid).'' TW `.tid` field syntax allows ONE line per field — the next non-`name: value` line is treated as body content. 0.0.1's `take-call.tid` had two `<$action-sendmessage>` widgets separated by a literal newline inside `ca-actions`; only `clear-context` actually fired. Same defect in `start-meeting.tid` `ca-leader-actions` — `clear-context` fired but `set-view` did not, so `m` cleared the context without switching to the pick-attendees view. Both files now concatenate the two action widgets onto one line. ''(2) Per-topic intersection in `topics-for-context.tid` (NEW `macros.tid`).'' 0.0.1's view filter used `:filter[<currentTiddler>get[stakeholders]enlist-input[] +[enlist<sticky-context-list>]]` — incorrect because `+[enlist<X>]` REPLACES the accumulator with the enlist'd titles (the `+` prefix sets source = prior, but `enlist<X>` is a source-emitter and ignores its source), silently matching every topic. Fixed by extracting a `\function worga.any-pinned-stakeholder(topic)` into the new `macros.tid` (tagged `$:/tags/Macro`, picked up by cp's startup `\import`) that uses the proper `:intersection[enlist<sticky-context-list>]` per-topic. View tiddler now calls `:filter[function[worga.any-pinned-stakeholder],<currentTiddler>]` (explicit-arg form per the `tw-gotchas-widget-context#filter functions and <currentTiddler> binding` defensive recommendation). Verified at the CLI level that nested-bracket inline `:intersection` inside `:filter[predicate]` silently produces wrong results — extracting to a named function bypasses the parser issue AND makes the helper reusable. ''Touches:'' `actions/take-call.tid`, `leaders/start-meeting.tid`, new `macros.tid`, `views/topics-for-context.tid`, `readme.tid`, `doc/overview.tid`, `plugin.info`, `changelog.tid`. JS modules unchanged; tiddler restart required for the new shadow values to land. |

What it is

A small ''workday + orga'' workflow layer on top of ''`rimir/cascade-palette`''. Three shipped tiddlers + one worked-example view demonstrate how to wire pin-people / start-meeting flows into cp's [[sticky-context|$:/plugins/rimir/cascade-palette/help/sticky-context]] mechanism. The plugin is intentionally minimal — bring your own data model and adapt the filters.

! Mechanism vs workflow split

* ''`rimir/cascade-palette`'' (mechanism). Ships the sticky-context state tiddler, the Context pill strip, the universal Pin / Unpin / Clear verbs, and the `<<sticky-context-list>>` / `<<sticky-context-count>>` variables exposed to every filter eval. Also ships the engine support that makes worga's views work: `ca-view-after-fire: stay` (0.0.96), ambient `<<sticky-context-list>>` in every `_filterInScope` call (0.0.97), and the view-history back-stack so Esc out of `m`-driven or take-call-driven views returns to where you were (0.0.98) — without those, multiselect views and context-aware row-template filters silently fail and side-quest navigation feels like a dead end.
* ''`rimir/worga`'' (workflow). Ships ''Take call from this person'' (creates a running `conversation` and drills into it), ''In context of participants…'' (a conversation-scoped drill over the participants' work items + topics, with inline create), ''Start meeting'' (`m` leader), a ''Pick attendees'' toggle-multiselect view, and a ''Topics for context'' worked example. The sticky-context pieces work standalone; the conversation verbs additionally require `rimir/kind` (≥0.1.70) + cascade-palette's `drill-sequence` message (≥0.0.124).

! Shipped tiddlers

|!Tiddler |!What it does |!Field of interest |
|`actions/take-call.tid` |Single-keystroke "I'm on a call with this person" — creates a running `conversation` (parent + participant = the person, `planned-at: now`, dated caption) and drills into it |`ca-after-fire: keep` keeps palette open; action sets the draft, runs `kind.apply-defaults-to` + `kind.finalize-create`, then fires `rimir-cascade-palette-drill-sequence` so the conversation's action menu lands on top with the person's conversation list as pop-target |
|`actions/conversation-context.tid` |''In context of participants…'' — on a `conversation`, drills into the open work items (clustered by Waiting for / Assignee / Stakeholder) and stakeholder topics referencing its participants, plus inline ''New Project / Task / Todo / Topic…'' create rows |`ca-items-from: [function[worga.context-items],<parent-picked>]`; rows + create logic live in `macros.tid`, reusing kind's `referencing-instances` / `instance-row-json` / `apply-defaults-to` / `finalize-create` |
|`leaders/start-meeting.tid` |`m` leader — clears context, activates the ''Pick attendees'' view |Wired via `rimir-cascade-palette-set-view` so the pick view becomes active immediately |
|`views/pick-attendees.tid` |Multiselect: Enter toggles each row in/out of sticky context. Pinned rows float to top, marked ☑ |`ca-view-after-fire: stay` (view-wide keep-open); `ca-view-row-icon` = ☑/☐ filter; `ca-view-sort-key` floats pinned to top; `ca-view-row-actions` uses inline-filter `{{{ ... }}}` on `$message` to dispatch pin-or-unpin from one widget |
|`views/topics-for-context.tid` |Worked example of a context-aware view — narrows to topics whose stakeholders intersect with pinned tiddlers |`ca-view-context-aware: yes` + the `worga.any-pinned-stakeholder` `\function` (in `macros.tid`, tagged `$:/tags/Macro`, picked up by cp's startup `\import`) — uses `:intersection[enlist<sticky-context-list>]` for proper set-intersection (the `+[enlist<X>]` shape REPLACES not intersects: `+` makes source = prior results, but `enlist<X>` is source-emitting and ignores its source) |

! The pick-attendees toggle pattern

The 0.0.5+ shape demonstrates a reusable multiselect pattern. Three coordinated overrides:

* ''Row icon'' (`ca-view-row-icon: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[☑]else[☐]]`) — pinned rows show ☑, unpinned show ☐. Re-evaluates on every stage recompute (which fires after every pin/unpin action) so the visual mirrors state live.
* ''Sort key'' (`ca-view-sort: custom` + `ca-view-sort-key: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[0]else[1]addsuffix<currentTiddler>]`) — produces "0<title>" for pinned rows, "1<title>" for unpinned. localeCompare puts "0" before "1", so pinned float to the top; title is the alphabetic tiebreaker within each group.
* ''Toggle action'' (`ca-view-row-actions: <$action-sendmessage $message={{{ ... }}} title=<<currentTiddler>>/>`) — single widget. The `$message` attribute is an inline filter that picks `rimir-cascade-palette-unpin-context` when the row is already pinned, `rimir-cascade-palette-pin-context` otherwise. Same `title` parameter for both messages so no branching needed outside `$message`.

All three rely on cascade-palette 0.0.97's ambient `<<sticky-context-list>>` (the per-row template filters are evaluated via `_filterInScope` and need the variable in scope) AND on 0.0.96's `ca-view-after-fire: stay` (so the palette doesn't close between toggles).

! Config tiddlers

Three knobs let you adapt the shipped views to your data model without forking:

* `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-stakeholder-field` — field name read by ''Topics for context'' (default `stakeholders`). If your topics use `stakeholder` (singular), `assignee`, `owner`, etc., change it here.
* `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-roots-filter` — base "topics" filter (default `[all[tiddlers]has[stakeholders]]`). If you have a typed model, scope to it: e.g. `[all[tiddlers]field:kind.type[topic]]`.
* `$:/config/rimir/worga/attendees-roots-filter` — base "persons" filter for ''Pick attendees'' (default unions kind-typed and tag-typed persons, both with `!is[system]` to keep kind's self-describing type-definition tiddlers out of the picker).

! Adding your own workflow

The pattern is:

# Add an ''action tiddler'' tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/action` whose `ca-applies` matches the rows where the verb should appear, and whose `ca-actions` sends the right cp messages. Add `ca-after-fire: keep` if you want the palette to stay open after firing.
# Add a ''leader'' tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/leader` with a single-char key and an action chain.
# Add a ''view'' tagged `$:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view` that consumes `<<sticky-context-list>>` in its `ca-view-roots` / `ca-layer-children` filter AND declares `ca-view-context-aware: yes` so the badge appears. For multiselect-style views, also set `ca-view-after-fire: stay` and override `ca-view-row-icon` / `ca-view-sort-key` / `ca-view-row-actions` for the checkbox-style UX.

That's it — the cp engine does the rest.

\function worga.attendee-sort-key(row) [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<row>then[0]else[1]] :map[<row>get[caption]else<row>addprefix[ ]addprefix<currentTiddler>]

<!-- Conversation rows referencing a person, for the take-call drill-sequence
     landing. Reuses kind's reverse-nav row builder for the conversation×participants
     relation, so the rows carry status grouping + the real title (action menu). -->
\function worga.call-conversations(person) [function[kind.locate-type],[conversation]] +[first[]] :map:flat[function[kind.instance-rows-for-pair],<person>,<currentTiddler>,[participants]]

<!-- In-context-of-conversation drill: from a conversation, surface the open
     work items and topics that reference its participants. Two-hop reverse-ref
     (conversation -> participants -> referencing instances), grouped by role.
     Reuses kind's referencing-instances + instance-row-json so there's no
     duplication of the reverse-ref / row-building logic. -->

<!-- Participants are persons or teams; expand each team to its member persons
     (the role fields below only ever reference persons). -->
\function worga.expand-participant(p) [<p>get[kind.type]match[team]] :map:flat[<p>get[members]enlist-input[]] ~[<p>]
\function worga.conv-persons(conv) [<conv>get[participants]enlist-input[]] :map:flat[function[worga.expand-participant],<currentTiddler>] +[unique[]]

<!-- Open = not archived and not completed (project/task/todo express "done"
     via completed-date; topics only have active/archived). -->
\function worga.is-open(inst) [<inst>!has[completed-date]] :filter[<currentTiddler>get[status]!match[archived]]

<!-- Effective date for within-group ordering (date fields store YYYYMMDD,
     so a lexical sort is chronological); fall back to modified for topics. -->
\function worga.ctx-date(inst) [<inst>get[due-date]!is[blank]] ~[<inst>get[follow-up-date]!is[blank]] ~[<inst>get[start-date]!is[blank]] ~[<inst>get[modified]!is[blank]] ~[<inst>]

\function worga.person-role-instances(person, field, kinds-csv) [enlist<kinds-csv>] :map:flat[function[kind.locate-type],<currentTiddler>] :map:flat[function[kind.referencing-instances],<person>,<currentTiddler>,<field>]
\function worga.role-instances(conv, field, kinds-csv) [function[worga.conv-persons],<conv>] :map:flat[function[worga.person-role-instances],<currentTiddler>,<field>,<kinds-csv>] :filter[function[worga.is-open],<currentTiddler>] +[unique[]]

\function worga.ctx-row-json(inst, label) [function[kind.resolve-ref],<inst>] ~[<inst>] :map[function[kind.instance-row-json],<inst>,<label>,<currentTiddler>]
\function worga.role-rows(conv, field, label, kinds-csv) [function[worga.role-instances],<conv>,<field>,<kinds-csv>] :map[function[worga.ctx-date],<currentTiddler>addsuffix[@@]addsuffix<currentTiddler>] +[sort[]] :map[<currentTiddler>split[@@]last[]] :map[function[worga.ctx-row-json],<currentTiddler>,<label>]

<!-- Create-in-context rows: one bind-less `ca-kind:text` row per creatable
     kind. The user types a caption; ca-on-commit fires worga.create-in-context
     with <<picked>> (the caption) and <<parent-picked>> (the conversation).
     Label + icon come from the kind def; threaded through -2/-3 because a
     \function can't interpolate a computed value into an addsuffix operand.
     The on-commit wikitext contains no [ ] so it needs no _brackets dance,
     only \" to escape the JSON-internal quotes. -->
\function worga.ctx-create-label(kind-key) [function[kind.locate-type],<kind-key>get[kind.caption]] ~[<kind-key>] +[addprefix[New ]]
\function worga.ctx-create-icon(kind-key) [function[kind.locate-type],<kind-key>get[kind.icon]] ~[[➕]]
\function worga.ctx-create-row(kind-key) [function[worga.ctx-create-label],<kind-key>] :map[function[worga.ctx-create-row-2],<kind-key>,<currentTiddler>]
\function worga.ctx-create-row-2(kind-key, label) [function[worga.ctx-create-icon],<kind-key>] :map[function[worga.ctx-create-row-3],<kind-key>,<label>,<currentTiddler>]
\function worga.ctx-create-row-3(kind-key, label, icon) [<label>] +[addprefix[{"ca-name":"]] +[addsuffix[…","ca-icon":"]] +[addsuffix<icon>] +[addsuffix[","ca-group":"Create","ca-hint":"Type a caption and ↵ — parent = this conversation, stakeholders = its participants.","ca-kind":"text","ca-on-commit":"<$transclude $variable=\"worga.create-in-context\" conv=<<parent-picked>> kind-key=\"]] +[addsuffix<kind-key>] +[addsuffix[\" caption=<<picked>>/>"}]]

<!-- Role-major emission: reorderByGroup keeps first-appearance group order and
     stable within-group order, so the runs become clusters in this sequence,
     each already date-sorted. The Create cluster trails the listings. -->
\function worga.context-items(conv) [function[worga.role-rows],<conv>,[waiting-for],[Waiting for],[project task todo]] [function[worga.role-rows],<conv>,[assignee],[Assignee],[project task todo]] [function[worga.role-rows],<conv>,[stakeholder],[Stakeholder],[project task todo]] [function[worga.role-rows],<conv>,[stakeholder],[Topics],[topic]] [function[worga.ctx-create-row],[project]] [function[worga.ctx-create-row],[task]] [function[worga.ctx-create-row],[todo]] [function[worga.ctx-create-row],[topic]]

<!-- Create a new instance of <<kind-key>> parented to the conversation, with
     the conversation's participants (teams expanded to member persons, since
     stakeholder only ref-types person) as stakeholders and the typed caption.
     Defaults fill the rest; finalize-create derives the title from the kind's
     title-formula. apply-defaults is idempotent so the pre-set fields survive.
     The drill recomputes after commit, so the new item appears in its group. -->
\procedure worga.create-in-context(conv, kind-key, caption)
<$let kind-tid={{{ [function[kind.locate-type],<kind-key>] }}} draft-tid="$:/state/rimir/worga/ctx-create/draft">
<$action-setfield $tiddler=<<draft-tid>> parent=<<conv>> caption=<<caption>> stakeholder={{{ [function[worga.conv-persons],<conv>] +[join[ ]] }}}/>
<$transclude $variable="kind.apply-defaults-to" type-tid=<<kind-tid>> target-tid=<<draft-tid>>/>
<$transclude $variable="kind.finalize-create" kind-tid=<<kind-tid>> kind-type-key=<<kind-key>> draft-tid=<<draft-tid>> savetitle="$:/state/rimir/worga/ctx-create/result"/>
<$action-deletetiddler $tiddler=<<draft-tid>>/>
</$let>
\end

Workday (`wor`) + organisational (`ga`) workflows layered on top of `rimir/cascade-palette` and `rimir/kind`. Demonstrates two integration patterns: (1) cp's sticky-context mechanism — pin people during a meeting, then watch context-aware views narrow to topics / tasks / notes involving the pinned set; and (2) conversation-centric verbs over a kind data model — take a call (creates a running conversation and drills into it), then surface and create the work items / topics in the context of its participants.

The plugin is intentionally small. It demonstrates the integration pattern; bring your own data model (kind, orga-data-model, hand-rolled tags) and adapt the filters via the three shipped config tiddlers to match your fields.

!! Key features

* ''`Take call from this person`'' action — Space on a person row → fires the verb → ''creates a running `conversation`'' (a `rimir/kind` instance) parented to the person, with that person as participant, `planned-at: now` and a `Conversation at <date time>` caption, then ''drills into the new conversation'' in the palette: the conversation's action menu sits on top, and popping out reveals the person's ''Referenced by…'' conversation list, then wherever you came from. Palette stays open (`ca-after-fire: keep`). Uses cascade-palette's `drill-sequence` message + `rimir/kind`'s reverse-nav + create procedures. Surfaces on rows with `kind.type: person` AND on any tiddler tagged `Person`.
* ''`In context of participants…`'' action — on a `conversation` row, drills into the open work items and topics that reference the conversation's participants (teams expanded to member persons). Projects / tasks / todos are clustered by role — ''Waiting for'', ''Assignee'', ''Stakeholder'' — and stakeholder ''Topics'' get their own cluster; each is sorted soonest-actionable first (done / archived items excluded). The same drill carries ''New Project / Task / Todo / Topic…'' rows: type a caption and ↵ to create one parented to the conversation, with the participants as stakeholders — it reappears in its cluster on the spot.
* ''`Start meeting`'' leader — bound to ''`m`''. Clears the sticky context and opens the ''Pick attendees'' view.
* ''`Pick attendees`'' view — a checkbox-style multiselect. Each row carries a ☑/☐ row icon mirroring whether that person is currently in sticky context. Enter toggles in/out of the context. Pinned rows float to the top. Esc closes the picker; the populated context survives.
* ''`Topics for context`'' view — worked example of a context-aware view. Layer filter narrows to topics whose `stakeholders` field contains at least one pinned tiddler. Declares `ca-view-context-aware: yes` so the view pill paints an indigo badge when context is non-empty. Edit `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-stakeholder-field` to match your data model.

!! Prerequisites

* TiddlyWiki ≥ 5.4.0
* `rimir/cascade-palette` ≥ 0.0.124 — provides sticky-context + the view machinery as before (0.0.96–0.0.98), plus the `rimir-cascade-palette-drill-sequence` message (0.0.124) that `Take call` uses to create-then-land-in-context. Without 0.0.124 the `Take call` landing falls back to a no-op (the conversation is still created).
* `rimir/kind` ≥ 0.1.70 — ''required'' for `Take call` and `In context of participants…` (they create / list `kind` instances and reuse kind's reverse-nav + create procedures). A `conversation` type plus `project` / `task` / `todo` / `topic` / `person` / `team` types with the expected fields (`participants`, `parent`, `stakeholder`, `assignee`, `waiting-for`, `status`) must exist in your wiki. The `Pick attendees` / `Topics for context` flows still work tag-based without kind.

!! Quick start

# Install `rimir/cascade-palette` 0.0.124+, `rimir/kind` 0.1.70+ and this plugin. Restart.
# Open the palette (Ctrl-Space). The Context pill strip is empty.
# In any view, Space on a tiddler representing a person — pick ''Take call from this person''. A running `conversation` is created parented to the person, and the palette drills into it: you land on the conversation's action menu. From there, drill ''In context of participants…'' to see the work items / topics involving the participants — or create new ones inline. Press ''`Esc`'' to pop back to the person's conversation list, then to where you came from.
# To start a multi-person meeting: type `m` (leader) → the ''Pick attendees'' view opens. Enter on each attendee — each toggles in/out of context, view stays open, ☑/☐ updates live, pinned rows float to top. ''`Esc`'' returns to the view you were in when you pressed `m` (the picked attendees stay in sticky context).
# Type ''`C`'' (capital, leader) to clear sticky context.

!! Adding your own context-aware views

The mechanism is in cp; this plugin is just patterns. To add your own view that narrows by sticky context:

```
title: $:/your/views/whatever
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view
ca-view-name: My narrowed view
ca-view-context-aware: yes
ca-view-roots: [all[tiddlers]has[<your-field>]] :filter[<currentTiddler>get[<your-field>]enlist-input[] :intersection[enlist<sticky-context-list>]]
```

The badge appears when sticky context is non-empty AND `ca-view-context-aware: yes`. The narrowing happens in the filter — there's no engine-level auto-narrow.

!! Adding your own toggle-multiselect

For a checkbox-style multiselect view (the pattern Pick attendees uses):

```
title: $:/your/views/multiselect
tags: $:/tags/rimir/cascade-palette/view
ca-view-name: Pick X
ca-view-roots: [all[tiddlers]field:kind.type[YOUR-TYPE]!is[system]]
ca-view-sort: custom
ca-view-sort-key: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[0]else[1]addsuffix<currentTiddler>]
ca-view-row-icon: [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[☑]else[☐]]
ca-view-after-fire: stay
ca-view-row-actions: <$action-sendmessage $message={{{ [enlist<sticky-context-list>match<currentTiddler>then[rimir-cascade-palette-unpin-context]else[rimir-cascade-palette-pin-context]] }}} title=<<currentTiddler>>/>
```

Two patterns coordinate: the row-icon + sort-key give visual state; the inline-filter `$message` toggles per row. Enter on any row pins or unpins; the palette stays open between toggles thanks to `ca-view-after-fire: stay`.

Two config tiddlers customise the shipped verbs and views without forking the plugin.

! `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-stakeholder-field`

Field name read by ''Topics for context'' when deciding which topics involve a pinned person. Default `stakeholders`. Change to match your data model (e.g. `attendees`, `participants`, `team-member-of`).

<$edit-text tiddler="$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-stakeholder-field" tag="input" default="stakeholders"/>

! `$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-roots-filter`

Override the base "topics" filter used by ''Topics for context''. Default `[all[tiddlers]has[stakeholders]]`. Change to match how your topics are tagged / typed (e.g. `[all[tiddlers]has[kind.type]get[kind.type]match[topic]]`).

<$edit-text tiddler="$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-roots-filter" tag="input" default="[all[tiddlers]has[stakeholders]]"/>

! `$:/config/rimir/worga/attendees-roots-filter`

Source filter for the ''Pick attendees'' view (drilled into by the ''Start meeting'' leader). Default unions kind-typed persons and tag-typed persons so a non-kind user still has results.

Narrows live as you pin / unpin.","ca-view-context-aware":"yes","ca-view-roots":"[subfilter{$:/config/rimir/worga/topics-roots-filter}] :filter[function[worga.any-pinned-stakeholder],<currentTiddler>]","ca-view-sort":"alphabetical","ca-order":"510"}}}
